d_sv_content.name: Using a combination of therapies for treatment of nasal cancer in dogs
d_sv_content.tagline: Help us find new treatments for dogs with nasal cancer!
d_sv_content.description: The purpose of this study is to prospectively evaluate the response of nasal cancer to a combination of therapies (chemotherapy and radiation therapy) in dogs.
d_sv_content.requirements: Dogs that are scheduled to receive radiation therapy for the treatment of nasal cancer can be enrolled in the study. Dogs will be placed into a group receiving radiation therapy alone or with chemotherapy.  Response to these treatments will be assessed with CT scans (done before and after treatment).
d_sv_content.responsibilities: You will be responsible for providing follow-up information to the treating clinicians and returning the dog 4 weeks after initiation of radiation therapy for a second CT evaluation (the first is performed prior to treatment).
d_sv_content.whoCan: We are looking for dogs diagnosed with nasal tumors.
d_sv_content.benefits: We hope that the data acquired in this study will allow us to advance the treatment of cancer in both pets and people.
d_sv_content.compensation: The CT scans, chemotherapy administration, and part of the radiation therapy will be paid for by the study.
d_sv_content.timeCommitment: We expect that participation in this clinical trial will last for 6 months (4 visits at Day 1, 14, 42 and 180).
